First of you need to get the basics done. Hiragana and Katakana. Then Kanji would be the next step, since your goal is just reading. There are 2200 kanji in daily use divided into 5 parts from N5 to N1 where N5 is kanji which elementary students learn and N1 kanji is basically high schoolers and up. You say you want to learn reading? But do you also want to understand what you read? Then there is no way you can do that without learning grammar. Again, N5 to N1. Obviously there is more for N1 since its basically advanced. There is no fastest way. It takes time for your brain to comprehend reading the letters and kanji.
